title: Swing-extreme primitive extraction -- non-blocking review follow-ups (round 2)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #206 (backend-swing-point-detector-followups, batched with backend-watchlist-breadth-proxy-followups and backend-profit-target-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md's §2 module-layout tree still wasn't updated to list the new app/signals/_swing_extremes.py module under signals/ -- this is the same recurring doc-completeness gap this very task's own checklist previously flagged (and marked done) for swing_points.py/support_resistance.py, now recurring for the new shared primitive module this PR itself introduced. Add it to the tree.

app.signals.support_resistance._find_swing_points calls rolling_extreme_masks twice (once for highs, once for lows), and each call computes BOTH a rolling max and a rolling min over the full series but discards one of the two results (is_swing_high, _ = rolling_extreme_masks(highs, ...) throws away the min; _, is_swing_low = rolling_extreme_masks(lows, ...) throws away the max) -- 4 rolling passes over the series where 2 would do. Not a correctness issue (flagged by code-review on PR #206), but an avoidable efficiency regression introduced by this exact refactor. Consider a mode='max'|'min'|'both' parameter (or two thin single-purpose wrappers) on rolling_extreme_masks so each caller only pays for the side it actually uses.
